name: Subor (小霸王)
blurb: China's best-known Famicom clone, later sold with a keyboard as a learning computer
title: Subor (小霸王): China's Famicom Clone and Learning Computer
description: Subor (Xiaobawang) is a Zhongshan, Guangdong brand whose cheap Famicom-compatible consoles and keyboard learning computers were everywhere in 1990s China.
h1: What was the Subor (小霸王) game console?
answer: Subor, in Chinese Xiaobawang (小霸王, "Little Conqueror"), was a Chinese electronics brand from Zhongshan, Guangdong, whose cheap clones of Nintendo's Famicom played the same cartridges at a fraction of the price. From around 1993 it added a keyboard and sold the machines to parents as "learning computers", with Jackie Chan in its TV ads. The brand faded after its founding manager left in 1995, China banned game consoles in 2000 and PCs spread; a Subor subsidiary was declared bankrupt in the early 2020s.

body: In the early 1990s an imported Famicom could cost up to 1,500 yuan in China, about a year's wages for an ordinary worker. Subor's consoles copied the Famicom hardware closely enough to run the same cartridges, usually multi-game carts, but cost far less. Wikipedia reports about 30 million Famicom clones sold in China by late 1995, and Subor was the best-known name.

The company grew out of a loss-making factory owned by Zhongshan's Yihua Group. Duan Yongping became its director in 1989; sources differ on whether the Xiaobawang name dates from 1989, 1991 or 1992. Its first famiclone, the D25, came out in 1991.

Around 1993 Subor bundled the console with a full keyboard and marketed it as a Chinese-English learning machine for typing and computer lessons. The first model was the SB-218. Parents bought it as an educational computer; children mostly put a game cartridge in. Jackie Chan fronted the TV ads with the line "同是天下父母心，望子成龙小霸王", roughly "all parents feel the same: hoping their child becomes a dragon, Xiaobawang", a pun on his Chinese name. People's Daily's magazine reported that Subor's market share in learning machines once reached about 80%.

head: Year
What happened
rows: Duan Yongping takes over the factory in Zhongshan
Keyboard learning machines, starting with the SB-218
Duan leaves and founds BBK Electronics in Dongguan

Subor Z+, an AMD-powered console PC, is announced but never goes on sale
Bankruptcy petition filed against Subor Culture Development

body: Losing Duan and much of his team in 1995 hurt the company badly. The 2000 console ban, home PCs and internet cafés then shrank the market for learning machines. The bankruptcy that followed the failed Z+ project was of the subsidiary Subor Culture Development; reports at the time said the Subor brand itself carried on. Original consoles and learning machines now turn up only second-hand.

faq.q: Is Subor the same as the Famicom?
faq.a: No. It is a Chinese clone that plays Famicom cartridges. Nintendo did not make or license it.
Roughly "Little Conqueror" or "Little Overlord". The Western name is Subor.

faq.q: What is the 小霸王 truck in Taiwan?
faq.a: In Taiwan 小霸王 is the local name of the Hyundai Porter light truck, which has nothing to do with the game console.
